ARABIC — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #3
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: ARABIC
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Intensive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Listening.

2. When practising Conversational Skills: Interviews, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational Skills: Interviews.

   C. Copy random text without understanding Conversational Skills: Interviews.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Conversational Skills: Interviews.

   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening: Translation and Transcription.

   C. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive Listening: Translation and Transcription.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Attentive Listening: Translation and Transcription.

7. In ARABIC, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   B. Only memorise without using the language
   C. Avoid speaking to classmates
   D. Mix random languages with no purpose

8. When practising Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
12. In three clear sentences, explain Verbs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Al mu’raab wal mabnii and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Active and Passive Verbs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Intensive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. (4 marks)
